newsitem.title: BRAZIL: African coffee officials to meet Brazilians Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: African coffee officials to meet Brazilians Dec 13.

text.p: The Ivory Coast's minister for commodities and five other African coffee officials are to meet representatives from Brazil's Industry and Commerce and Foreign Affairs ministry Friday, an Ivorian official said.
"Minister Guy-Alain Gauze has also asked that members of the coffee private sector which make up the coffee deliberative council should also be present," the official said.
The meeting is scheduled to take place at 1200 local/1400 GMT in Brasilia, he added.
The African delegation also includes the Ugandan Trade Minister and the Angolan Primary Commodities Secretary, the Ivorian embassy official said.

The group yesterday met Colombian officials in Bogota during which representatives agreed on a need to cut exports by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) by about 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first six months of 1997.
Under the plan agreed by ACPC members in May, exports in the January to June period of next year should not exceed 26.28 million bags.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
